title: Ada and the Tide
premise: Kestrel Underhill built his career on the belief that love is logistics — until a snowstorm traps him, his estranged ex, and the woman he once almost chose, all in a coastal inn where he's been hired to stage a wedding neither bride nor groom seems to want. As the storm cuts them off, old wounds reopen and Kestrel discovers the wedding is a cover for a family power struggle that once destroyed his own. When the truth of who orchestrated the weekend surfaces, Kestrel must choose between protecting his rebuilt heart and fighting for the found family the storm has forced together. He ends the novel risking everything — the wedding collapses, the truth detonates, and in the wreckage Kestrel finally lends his whole heart, not pieces.
about_author: Petra Ishikawa is a former event planner who spent a decade watching love get budgeted, contracted, and catered before turning to fiction. She writes from a small apartment above a flower shop, where the tide — and the weddings — come in daily.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Doesn't Break
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet him mid-wedding, flawlessly orchestrating a ceremony he privately disdains, training his heart like an athlete trains a muscle. A call from his estranged ex, Margot, offers a lucrative gig at a remote coastal inn — a wedding for a powerful family he recognizes from his past. Emotional beat: controlled detachment cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Contract
chapters.summary: Kestrel arrives at the inn and discovers the co-planner is Wren Calloway — his best mistake of their twenties, the woman who left when he chose ambition over her. The client family's cold patriarch watches them both with unsettling interest. POV alternates. Emotional beat: shock, hostility, and the first involuntary flicker of old warmth.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: A historic snowstorm seals the coastal road; the wedding party is stranded, including the bride, who seems strangely resigned, and the groom, who drinks alone. Kestrel and Wren must share the inn's last working suite of planning rooms. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and forced proximity turning rivalry into uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Bride Who Packed Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren notices the bride's suitcase is half empty — she isn't planning to stay. Digging for answers, Wren finds a second, older contract in the family files, one bearing Kestrel's father's name. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread, and a growing tenderness she resents herself for.

chapters.title: What the Storm Digs Up
chapters.summary: Power fails; candles, wine, and confession. Kestrel tells Wren how his family was ruined by the client patriarch years ago — and why he took this job: to buy back the family home. Wren admits she left to save herself, not to punish him. Emotional beat: the almost-kiss interrupted by the bride screaming in the snow.

chapters.title: Runaway in Reverse
chapters.summary: The bride begs them to help her flee; the groom, it emerges, knows and doesn't care — the marriage is a business merger. Kestrel realizes the wedding itself is the weapon, a public consolidation of assets. POV alternates. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — helping her means destroying Kestrel's chance at redemption.

chapters.title: The Price of the House
chapters.summary: The patriarch corners Kestrel: help deliver the wedding and the family home is his; interfere and he'll finish what he started. Kestrel, alone in the boathouse, nearly signs. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — power offered as a bribe, survival priced in complicity.

chapters.title: Everything We Bury, the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Wren finds the signed papers and believes Kestrel betrayed her and the bride both. She confronts him before the whole stranded party; the patriarch's manipulation is exposed in fragments. The bride announces the wedding is off. Emotional beat: the climax's first detonation — heartbreak, accusation, and Kestrel choosing, at last, to burn the contract.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Climax. Kestrel publicly exposes the patriarch's scheme using the family files Wren found, forfeiting the house and his father's name being cleared at a cost. The stranded guests, transformed into a found family by the storm, rally around the freed bride and groom. Emotional beat: ruin and release — losing everything except the people.

chapters.title: Whole Heart, Rising Tide
chapters.summary: Spring. The inn reopens under new ownership — the guests, pooled together. Kestrel plans one last wedding for free: the bride and groom, remarried on their own terms, with Wren as co-planner and co-conspirator. On the tide line, he offers his whole heart. POV alternates. Emotional beat: resolution — love uncontained, untrained, and finally worth the risk.
